transcript:
"This is NPR News Now, the latest headlines every hour."
Live from the NPR News in Washington, I'm Windsor Johnston.
President Trump says he's reached an agreement with Chinese President Xi Jinping on artificial
intelligence.
Trump says the two leaders have agreed to what he calls "joint guardrails for the technology."
NPR's Deepa Shivram reports the agreement comes as the U.S. and China are racing to
develop more powerful AI.
Trump briefed the press on this week's trip to China.
Talk of "guardrails" is a new move for Trump, who's always been adamant that the technology
should not have any regulations because it would hold the U.S. back in the race against
China on AI.
Now, he says sometimes the technology can be too powerful.
Neither country has released any further information on what those joint safeguards could look
like or how they would be implemented.
Trump also said he would continue to push for the construction of data centers in the
U.S. and will penalize companies that build them outside the U.S.
Deepa Shivram, NPR News, Washington.
The man accused of setting a deadly fire in Southern California last year has been found
guilty.
The blaze swept through the Pacific Palisades neighborhood of Los Angeles in January of
2025.
Steve Futterman reports.
The jury found Jonathan Rinderknecht, a former Uber driver, guilty of starting the Luckman
fire on January 1st last year.
That fire was never completely put out and smoldered underground for a week before reemerging
as the Palisades fire.
The defense suggested that the Luckman fire started from fireworks.
Juror number three, Cameron, who declined to give his last name, said everything implicated
Rinderknecht.
Strongest evidence was the defendant's own testimony stating that he was up on the hill
and see fireworks.
Logically, things start pointing towards him.
Conferencing is set for next March, Rinderknecht faces a maximum of 40 years in prison, meanwhile
numerous civil lawsuits accusing the city, utilities and others with negligence are still
pending.
For NPR News, I'm Steve Futterman at the Federal Courthouse in Los Angeles.
A storm forming off the east coast of Florida is expected to track northeast this weekend.
The National Hurricane Center says it could strengthen into a tropical or subtropical
storm.
In the last two inches, David Roth with the Weather Prediction Center says the rain will
spread into Georgia and the Carolinas.
So the forecast is for areas of one to two inches of rain across portions of Georgia
and coastal South Carolina, local maxima probably in the range of four inches.
So much lower than what Florida has had, but still wet.
The National Hurricane Center says strong gusts and dangerous surf are possible along
parts of the southeast and mid-Atlantic coast.
The risk of rip currents and coastal flooding could last in too early next week.
Stocks fell on Wall Street this week, led by a sell-off in companies tied to artificial
intelligence.
The tech-heavy NASDAQ gave up its gains for the year.
This is NPR News in Washington.
A second federal judge has blocked President Trump's plan to build a memorial arch in
the nation's capital.
Lawyers challenging the project say Friday's ruling in Virginia will keep construction
on hold while several lawsuits play out.
Two days earlier, a federal judge in Washington extended a temporary order barring the administration
from breaking ground.
The Virginia County Board sued over the project, saying it would make traffic worse and put
public safety at risk.
A planetary probe built by the European and Japanese space agencies is about to go into
orbit around Mercury.
Joe Palkall reports the spacecraft took more than eight years to reach its target.
The reason it took the probe known as BepiColombo so long to reach the innermost planet in our
solar system is basically because it had to slow down to keep from falling into the sun.
To do that, mission managers use the gravity of Earth, Venus, and Mercury itself to adjust
the spacecraft's velocity.
"We are approaching the planet with a very slow speed."
Ignacio Clerigo is the spacecraft operations manager for BepiColombo.
He says the probe is traveling about 670 miles per hour as it sneaks up on Mercury.
Once there, it will fire its main engines to enter orbit.
Its scientific mission to study the rocky planet will begin next spring.
For NPR News, I'm Joe Palkall.
New York City Mayor Zoran Mamdani says he's planning to close Rikers Island jail complex
by 2032.
The city is expected to miss its legal deadline to close Rikers and replace it with four smaller
jails by 2027.
This is NPR News.

Jonathan Rinderknecht found guilty of starting the 2025 Lunar fire that became the Palisades fire

Stocks fall on Wall Street led by AI-linked companies; NASDAQ gives up its gains for the year
Second federal judge in Virginia blocks Trump's memorial arch project in the nation's capital
European-Japanese BepiColombo probe nears Mercury, set to enter orbit after eight-year journey
